name: Kingdom of Uvea (1842–1860)
description: A white field bearing the monogram 'AM' in red and navy at the centre, with four small crosses in the corners — two red and two navy.
history: Devised by the Marist Father Pierre Bataillon for the customary kingdom of Uvea (Wallis) at the protectorate treaty signed with Captain Mallet on 4 November 1842. It was gradually superseded during the 1850s, a variant of 1860 following it, before the present Wallisian flag with the Maltese cross.

features.symbolism: the Marist mission's dedication to the Virgin Mary

features.role: crosses in the four corners, two red and two navy
